extracted.intended_audience: entrepreneurs, industrialists, financiers, and young businesspeople seeking practical guidance on negotiation, investment, and corporate conduct
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, experience-based standards for conducting high-level business negotiations, allocating capital, managing endorsements and partnerships, and running manufacturing operations with integrity and technical rigor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrity over cleverness / spirit over letter
rubrics_metrics.description: Not the letter of the law, but the spirit, must be the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reputation for 'cuteness' and sharp dealing is fatal in great affairs. Always give the other party the benefit of the doubt; correct mistakes promptly whether they favor your firm or the other party. Example: returned a $10,000 check to J.S. Morgan to preserve honor and trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Endorsement prudence (two essential questions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Have I surplus means for all possible requirements which will enable me to pay without inconvenience the utmost sum for which I am liable under this endorsement? Secondly: Am I willing to lose this sum for the friend for whom I endorse?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only endorse when both questions can be answered affirmatively. If you can pay the full amount, consider paying it then and there rather than exposing yourself to future risk. Keep partnership agreements that limit personal endorsement beyond trivial sums.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concentrate on one business / master your line
rubrics_metrics.description: I believe the true road to preëminent success in any line is to make yourself master in that line. 'Put all good eggs in one basket and then watch that basket.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus time and capital on the business you know best. Reinvest surplus earnings into your own operations (machinery, improved methods) rather than scattering investments across many unrelated enterprises. If extension in your business is not possible, put surplus into first-class securities for steady revenue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid speculative gambling; keep business honorable
rubrics_metrics.description: Stock gambling and honorable business are incompatible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between speculative markets (gamblers) and business operations; do not mix speculative behavior with the conduct of an honest manufacturing or trading enterprise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain calm and patience in financial panics
rubrics_metrics.description: When one party to a bargain becomes excited, the other should keep cool and patient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not be provoked into hasty action when counterparties panic. Example: postponed closing with Barings during the Bismarck panic; cooling-off might have preserved a more favorable agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer strategic alliances over litigation when timing matters
rubrics_metrics.description: When litigation would cause delay sufficient to lose market advantage, consider union or merger rather than asserting legal rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: rather than suing for patent infringement (which would take years), unite with a competitor (Pullman) to secure immediate control of the market and avoid losing the opportunity to a faster rival.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal courtesies and first offers to trusted partners
rubrics_metrics.description: Give the first offer to Junius S. Morgan; if he cannot buy, he often places you in contact with a friendly house.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain and reward trusted business relationships by offering them priority access to opportunities. This builds long-term reciprocal support (example: always give Morgan the first offer).

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct errors promptly and fairly (internal and external)
rubrics_metrics.description: A mistake made by any one in favor of the firm is corrected as promptly as if the error were in favor of the other party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish standards of prompt correction for bookkeeping and transactional errors to build trust and a reputation for fairness (example: returned an overpayment rather than accept it).

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect personal and family obligations when assuming liability
rubrics_metrics.description: A man's means are a trust to be sacredly held for his own creditors as long as he has debts and obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate endorsements and new liabilities in light of obligations to family, partners, and the firm's employees; do not assume risks that would imperil dependents or core business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use expert consultation and experimental testing in manufacturing
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek and apply outside technical expertise and validate changes through experiment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When faced with technical problems, consult recognized experts and perform comparative experiments before committing to costly changes. Example: resolved Lucy Furnace trouble by building small glass-model furnaces and testing two bell shapes as advised by Whitwell.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use securities and board influence strategically, but cautiously
rubrics_metrics.description: Control of securities and board representation can secure traffic and influence for related enterprises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acquire or control securities to obtain strategic influence (e.g., board seats) that further business objectives, but remain mindful of counterparty actions and do not overextend in financing that could jeopardize core operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be vigilant: many can be trusted, a few need watching
rubrics_metrics.description: Many men can be trusted, but a few need watching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stay alert to partners' and agents' conduct; verify arrangements and instructions (example: discovered proceeds of bonds had been appropriated by other parties), and structure transactions to limit exposure to opportunistic behavior.
